name: bodylake
description: Read-only access to your health data from the Apple Health app.

interface.longDescription:
Bodylake copies everything in the Apple Health app on your iPhone to a private database in Germany, so ChatGPT can answer questions about your own history: years of steps, sleep, heart rate, workouts and every other type the Apple Health app records.

Ask in plain words, for example how your resting heart rate changed over the last two years, or which month had your most steps. ChatGPT reads the data it needs and answers with your own numbers.

Bodylake only reads. It never changes or deletes anything, in the Apple Health app or in Bodylake, and it reads only your own account.

You need a Bodylake account, set up in the Bodylake iPhone app, which syncs your history. You sign in with your passkey and allow ChatGPT to read your data, and you can disconnect ChatGPT at any time in the Bodylake app under Connected AIs.
defaultPrompt: How has my resting heart rate changed over the last two years, by quarter?
Which month in the last two years had my most steps?
Show my monthly average HRV for the last two years.

positive.description: Resting heart rate trend by quarter
positive.prompt: How has my resting heart rate changed over the last two years, by quarter?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls describe_data, then query_sql, and answers with one resting heart rate figure per quarter from the review account’s data.

positive.prompt: Which month in the last two years had my most steps?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls describe_data, then query_sql, and answers with the month with the most steps and its total, summed from the step samples of the last two years from the review account’s data.

positive.prompt: Show my monthly average HRV for the last two years.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls describe_data, then query_sql, and answers with one HRV average per month from the review account’s data.

positive.prompt: What was my longest running streak?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls describe_data, then query_sql, and answers with the longest run of consecutive days with a running workout from the review account’s data.

positive.prompt: Which workouts did I do in the last 90 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls describe_data, then query_sql, and answers with a list of the workouts of the last 90 days from the review account’s data.

negative.description: General knowledge: Bodylake is not called
negative.prompt: What is a normal resting heart rate for adults?

negative.description: Bodylake cannot write: not called, or the answer says it only reads
negative.prompt: Log a 5 km run for today
Find a running shoe shop near me

publication.release_notes: First release: read-only access to your health data from the Apple Health app, through two tools, describe_data and query_sql.

de-DE.subtitle: Ihre Gesundheitsdaten, lesbar.
de-DE.description:
Bodylake kopiert alles aus der App „Health“ von Apple auf Ihrem iPhone in eine private Datenbank in Deutschland, damit ChatGPT Fragen zu Ihrem eigenen Verlauf beantworten kann. Das umfasst Schritte, Schlaf, Herzfrequenz und Trainings aus vielen Jahren sowie jeden anderen Datentyp, den die App „Health“ von Apple aufzeichnet.

Fragen Sie in einfachen Worten, zum Beispiel wie sich Ihre Ruheherzfrequenz in den letzten zwei Jahren verändert hat oder in welchem Monat Sie die meisten Schritte gemacht haben. ChatGPT liest die Daten, die es braucht, und antwortet mit Ihren eigenen Zahlen.

Bodylake liest nur. Es ändert oder löscht nichts, weder in der App „Health“ von Apple noch in Bodylake, und es greift ausschließlich auf Ihr eigenes Konto zu.

Sie brauchen ein Bodylake-Konto, das Sie in der Bodylake-App auf dem iPhone einrichten. Die App synchronisiert Ihren Verlauf. Sie melden sich mit Ihrem Passkey an und erlauben ChatGPT, Ihre Daten zu lesen, und Sie können ChatGPT jederzeit in der Bodylake-App unter „Verbundene KIs“ trennen.
